newsitem.title: UK: Businessmen say they make good politicos -- UK study.
newsitem.headline: Businessmen say they make good politicos -- UK study.

text.p: More than half of Britain's finance directors believe business people make better politicos than career politicians do, according to a study published on Thursday.
A survey of 200 British financial directors in Accountancy Age magazine found that 54 percent backed businessmen as politicians, while 34 percent were neutral, and some 12 percent vetoed the idea.
The poll came on the coattails of this month's appointment of British Petroleum Co Plc chairman Sir David Simon as Britain's new minister for trade and competitiveness in Europe.
Those financial directors who supported businessmen as politicians said the business community taught people to be "better focused" and "good team leaders".
But those who felt that civil servants made the better politicians said the whole process of government went against the ethos of business practice.
"Politics is all about how we treat poor people. Business is how we all get richer!" one dissenting financial director said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
